title: The Case File team
intro: Settled: residents, PGs and fellows are part of the treating doctor's team, are added to each Case File by the doctor (from any department), join with a code, get limited access and never sign. These questions settle how the code and the team work; what they may do inside is R03.

questions.question: You said residents join a Case File with a code: how should the code work?

options.label: Doctor picks, code confirms (Recommended)
options.description: The doctor picks the resident by name; Vaidyx makes a code only that person can use; entering it is their acceptance.

options.label: One code, any registered trainee
options.description: The doctor shares one code; any resident, PG or fellow with a login who enters it joins; the doctor sees who joined.

options.label: Code, then doctor approves
options.description: Anyone with the code asks to join; the doctor taps Approve for each.

questions.why: Settled (notes role-treating, role-resident): the treating doctor adds residents per Case File from their own or other departments, and they join with a code. I03 liked. Today residents use the consultant's login (G14).

questions.question: Who may add a resident to a Case File and create the code?

options.label: Any owner-department consultant (Recommended)
options.description: Covers leave and OPD days; each addition is audited with the name of who added whom.

options.label: Only the doctor who created it
options.description: One person controls the team; when they are away nobody can add.

options.label: Creator and head of department
options.description: The head can step in; other consultants cannot.

questions.why: A Case File is created by one treating doctor and owned by that doctor's department (settled; access.py, B2). What residents may then do is R03.
questions.answer: Any consultant of the owner's team (Recommended)
questions.notes: Options adapted to R03-Q01 (owner consultant and co-owner consultant).

questions.question: Settled: each treating doctor has at least one resident. Who keeps each doctor's 'my residents' list current?

options.label: Admin sets, consultant adds (Recommended)
options.description: The department admin updates it when postings change; the consultant can add a resident too.

options.label: Only the department admin
options.description: One list kept by the department office; the consultant asks for changes.

options.label: Only the consultant
options.description: The doctor manages their own team; the office has no part.

questions.why: Settled (notes role-treating: each treating doctor linked with at least one PG, fellow or resident). Residents change units with postings. This list decides who is offered first when adding (R06-Q04). Builds on R04-Q02 (who creates trainee logins).

questions.question: When a doctor creates a Case File, should their own residents be pre-ticked for its team?

options.label: Pre-ticked, doctor can untick (Recommended)
options.description: Codes are made on Create; the team exists from the first minute with one step less.

options.label: Listed but not ticked
options.description: The create form shows them; the doctor ticks each one.

options.label: Only after creation
options.description: The team is added later from the Case File page.

questions.why: Answers whether a resident can be on a Case File from its creation. Settled: the treating doctor adds residents per Case File; a pre-tick is still the doctor's choice. UX note 1 (sensible defaults).

questions.question: When you add a resident or fellow from another department, who else must know or agree?

options.label: Their consultant is told (Recommended)
options.description: The code is enough; the trainee's own consultant gets a note, with nothing to approve.

options.label: Nobody, the code is enough
options.description: No one else hears about it.

options.label: Their head of department approves
options.description: The trainee joins only after their head of department approves.

questions.why: Settled: fellows from other departments may be added (notes role-treating). Their access is the same limited role (R03).
questions.own_words: The resident gets added to their doctor's Case File: the doctor shares the code with everyone, the resident enters it, the doctor approves, and that is it, they are in.

questions.question: What should the join code look like?

options.label: Six digits, like meetings (Recommended)
options.description: One pattern for everyone, easy to read out or type on a phone; labelled 'Case File code' so it is not mixed up with a meeting code.

options.label: Eight letters and digits
options.description: Harder to guess; harder to read out over the phone.

options.label: A link plus six digits
options.description: Tap the link on the phone, or type the digits.

questions.why: Settled: board members join meetings with a six-digit code (R11). One code style keeps things simple (notes plan, screens).

questions.question: How should the code reach the resident?

options.label: Doctor shares it (Recommended)
options.description: Vaidyx shows the code to the doctor, who reads it out or sends it any way; the code carries no patient data.

options.label: SMS from Vaidyx
options.description: Sent to the resident's mobile; needs the SMS gateway of R04-Q04.

options.label: WhatsApp from Vaidyx
options.description: Needs a WhatsApp Business account, a paid outside service.

questions.why: Vaidyx sends no SMS, email or WhatsApp today; notifications are in-app first (changes_v2 section 3). Channels in general are R14.

questions.question: How long should an unused join code stay valid?

options.label: 24 hours (Recommended)
options.description: Enough for a busy day; an expired code is made again with one tap.

options.label: 7 days
options.description: Covers weekends and leave; an old code lingers longer.

options.label: 15 minutes
options.description: Like an OTP; the resident must be at hand.

options.label: Until the doctor cancels it
options.description: Never expires by itself.

questions.why: No join code exists today. A short life limits a code passed on by mistake; one-tap re-issue keeps it cheap (UX note 12, a response for every state).

questions.question: Can one join code be used by more than one person?

options.label: Single use (Recommended)
options.description: Each code admits one person once, then stops working.

options.label: Reusable until it expires
options.description: One code for a whole batch of residents on the same Case File.

questions.why: Only open when the code is not tied to a named person (R06-Q01).
questions.skip_if: Skip if R06-Q01 answered 'Doctor picks, code confirms' (that code is single use for one named person).
questions.notes: Settled by R06-Q01 and R06-Q05: one code shared with the whole team, each person who enters it is approved by the doctor.

questions.question: Can a code bring in someone with no Vaidyx login, such as a visiting fellow or observer?

options.label: No, a login comes first (Recommended)
options.description: The department admin creates the login, then the code works; every action has a known name.

options.label: Yes, a temporary guest login
options.description: The code creates a login that ends with the Case File or after 30 days.

questions.why: Settled: the doctor adds residents 'registered in their respective department' (notes role-treating). R04-Q02 decides who creates trainee logins; R15 covers outside people seeing patient data.

questions.question: Who can end a resident's place on a Case File?

options.label: The doctors who can add (Recommended)
options.description: Removal follows the R06-Q02 rule, with a confirmation; the resident is told.

options.label: The resident, by leaving
options.description: They can step off a Case File themselves; the doctor is told.

options.label: The MDT Coordinator
options.description: Can tidy teams before a board session.

options.label: The department admin
options.description: Can remove a trainee who has left the unit from all its Case Files at once.

questions.why: No resident role exists today; removals act without confirmation (U07). What access remains when someone leaves a department is R03.
questions.answer: The consultants who can add; The resident, by leaving; The department admin

questions.question: Can one resident be on the Case Files of several consultants at once?

options.label: Yes, any number (Recommended)
options.description: Their home lists every Case File they joined, grouped by consultant.

options.label: Yes, up to a set number
options.description: A cap per resident, for example 20 open Case Files; a code beyond it is refused.

questions.why: Residents carry much of the preparation (role-resident: 39% to 72% of preparation hours in US data). Settled: fellows from other departments may join, so a resident may serve several consultants.

questions.question: When a Case File is referred to another department, what happens to the residents on it?

options.label: Read-only, like their department (Recommended)
options.description: They keep reading as the referring department does but can no longer prepare anything; the new owner adds their own team.

options.label: They leave the Case File
options.description: Their access ends when the referral is accepted.

options.label: They keep their place
options.description: The new owner decides whether to remove them.

questions.why: On acceptance ownership moves and the referring department stays a read-only participant (B10, DESIGN V2 Phase 5).

questions.question: Which events should reach a resident on a Case File?

options.label: Added or removed (Recommended)
options.description: They hear when they join, leave or are removed.

options.label: A department answered
options.description: A Done or an arriving record, so they can continue preparing.

options.label: Their draft approved or returned
options.description: The consultant's answer on what they prepared.

options.label: Listed for a board date
options.description: The date and session, so they can prepare to present.

questions.why: Residents get nothing today (no role). The owner liked I15 (re-fetch from the notification) and I16 (next-step card). Channels, grouping and quiet hours are R14; who approves drafts is R09.
questions.answer: Approved or removed; A department answered; Their proposal approved or returned; Listed for a board date
questions.notes: First option adapted to R06-Q01 (approval flow): 'approved or removed'.
